questions.question: How does sentence_split divide "First fact. Second fact!"?
options: ["First", "fact", "Second", "fact"]
["First fact. Second fact!"]
["First fact.", "Second fact!"]
["First fact", "Second fact"] without punctuation
questions.explanation: The regex splits after ., !, or ? followed by whitespace and keeps each sentence ending punctuation.

questions.question: What does similarity(s1, s2) measure in this TextRank implementation?
options: Cosine similarity between learned transformer embeddings
The edit distance between the two raw strings
The number of sentences between s1 and s2
Word-count overlap divided by a logarithmic function of the two vocabulary sizes
questions.explanation: It builds Counters from lowercase words, sums their intersection, and divides by log(len(w1)+1)+log(len(w2)+1).

questions.question: What does textrank return when the document has at most top_k sentences?
options: All parsed sentences in their original order
An empty list because ranking is unnecessary
Only the first top_k-1 sentences
A random sample of top_k sentences
questions.explanation: The early n <= top_k branch returns sentences directly rather than constructing a graph.

questions.question: Why does textrank sort the selected sentence indices after ranking them?
options: It makes every sentence have the same graph score
It preserves the original document order in the extractive summary
It removes sentences whose score is zero
It sorts words alphabetically inside each sentence
questions.explanation: The score ranking chooses important indices; a second sort makes the extracted text readable in source order.

questions.question: What denominator does rouge_n use for its overlap score?
options: The total number of hypothesis n-grams
The number of sentences in the article
The total number of reference n-grams
The vocabulary size of the corpus
questions.explanation: The implementation divides clipped overlap by sum(ref_ngrams.values()), making this a reference-coverage recall.

questions.question: What is the central difference between the demo TextRank and an abstractive summarizer?
options: TextRank translates sentences and abstractive models only count words
TextRank requires labels for every sentence, while abstractive models do not read text
They are identical except for the output file extension
TextRank selects source sentences, while an abstractive model can generate new wording
questions.explanation: The code returns selected original strings; rewriting content requires a generation model rather than sentence extraction.
